title: Committee of Supply debate on the Prime Minister's Office budget
what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head U (Prime Minister's Office) of the Estimates, with MPs moving cuts and ministers responding on public service, research and innovation, climate policy, population, cash and banking access, and insurance.
stage: Committee of Supply debate on Head U of the Estimates
why_it_matters: The transcript states that the carbon tax has increased to $45 per tonne this year, that households will receive additional U-Save rebates to manage energy costs, and that HDB has given the go-ahead for DBS to set up an ATM at Rivervale Shores. It also records that MAS is monitoring cash acceptance and may consider making cash acceptance mandatory by law.

key_points.point: Mr Foo Cexiang moved to reduce the allocation for Head U of the Estimates by $100.
key_points.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
key_points.quote: That the total sum to be allocated for Head U of the Estimates be reduced by $100.

key_points.point: Mr Foo Cexiang asked how the Public Service is preparing officers for a changing domestic landscape and a fracturing world order.
key_points.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
key_points.quote: how is the Public Service preparing our officers to better understand and meet the challenges posed by a changing domestic landscape

key_points.point: Ms He Ting Ru asked how Singapore guides and monitors executive discretion and what safeguards ensure it is done judiciously.
key_points.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
key_points.quote: how does Singapore guide and monitor the use of executive discretion and what are the safeguards in place to ensure that these are done judiciously?

key_points.point: Ms He Ting Ru proposed a central public registry of ministerial powers and delegated authorities.
key_points.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
key_points.quote: We should have a central public registry to record Ministerial powers and delegated authorities

key_points.point: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari asked how awareness, matching and role clarity for the GRIT@Gov programme can be strengthened.
key_points.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari
key_points.quote: how can awareness, matching and role clarity be better strengthened

key_points.point: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari asked how the Government will apply early resolution and mediation principles to workplace grievances.
key_points.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari
key_points.quote: how will the Government apply the principles of early resolution and mediation

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said the Public Service must understand the world, people and technology well.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: we must do three things well: understand the world well; understand our people well; and understand technology well.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said overseas postings and exchanges are being ramped up.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: we are ramping up overseas postings and exchanges, attachments to international organisations and stints in the private and people sectors.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said agencies received over 1,600 partnership proposals in 2025.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: In 2025, agencies received over 1,600 partnership proposals from citizens, corporates, community groups and organisations.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said 99% of government-to-citizen transactions can be completed digitally.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: Today, 99% of government-to-citizen transactions, like Community Development Council (CDC) vouchers, can be completed digitally.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said more than 4,300 officers from over 69 public agencies have gone through the Career Fitness Movement foundational programme.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: more than 4,300 officers from over 69 public agencies have gone through the foundational programme under the movement.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said the Public Service has a Grievance Handling Procedure and Internal Disclosure Policy.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: We have in place a Grievance Handling Procedure and Internal Disclosure Policy.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said all public officers must undergo compulsory digital and AI training.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: all public officers are required to undergo compulsory digital and AI training

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said all statutory functions must be exercised in accordance with the law.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: All statutory functions must be exercised in accordance with the law.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said the most important issues are referred to and discussed by Cabinet before a final decision.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: The most important issues are referred to and discussed by Cabinet before a final decision is taken.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said every decision and its grounds are carefully recorded.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: for every decision made, actually it is carefully recorded and the grounds of the decision made are carefully recorded.

key_points.point: Dr Choo Pei Ling said the $37 billion RIE2030 commitment is a deliberate investment.
key_points.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
key_points.quote: The Government’s $37 billion commitment under Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2030 (RIE2030) Plan

key_points.point: Dr Choo Pei Ling identified two priorities: anchoring value from innovation and sustaining renewal in the talent system.
key_points.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
key_points.quote: First, anchoring and capturing value from innovation. Second, sustaining renewal within our talent system.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said new RIE Flagships and RIE Grand Challenges will be launched.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: We will launch a number of new large-scale, cross-cutting RIE Flagships and RIE Grand Challenges.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said the Semiconductor RIE Flagship seeks to strengthen Singapore's position in the global semiconductor supply chain.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: The Semiconductor RIE Flagship seeks to strengthen Singapore's position as a strategic node in the global semiconductor supply chain

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said the RIE Grand Challenge on Maximising Healthy and Successful Longevity aims to support healthy ageing.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: The RIE Grand Challenge on Maximising Healthy and Successful Longevity

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said Singapore will accelerate nuclear safety research through the Singapore Nuclear Research and Safety Institute.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: We will also accelerate Singapore's nuclear safety research through the Singapore Nuclear Research and Safety Institute (SNRSI)

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said more than 60,000 jobs were associated with R&D activities in 2023.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: In 2023, more than 60,000 jobs were associated with R&D activities.

key_points.point: Ms Poh Li San asked about the impact of the United States' stance on Singapore's climate goals.
key_points.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
key_points.quote: what is the expected impact to Singapore's climate goals from the United States' (US') stance on climate

key_points.point: Ms Poh Li San asked about progress on domestic mitigation measures for the 2030 NDC target.
key_points.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
key_points.quote: what is the progress on Singapore's key domestic mitigation measures to meet our 2030 NDC target?

key_points.point: Mr Azhar Othman requested an update on progress towards net zero by 2050.
key_points.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman
key_points.quote: I would like to request an update from the Ministry regarding our progress towards achieving net zero by 2050.

key_points.point: Ms He Ting Ru asked how the Government ensures enough pressure on large emitters to decarbonise.
key_points.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
key_points.quote: how does the Government ensure that there is enough pressure on large emitters to decarbonise?

key_points.point: Mr Mark Lee asked how the Government assesses whether Singapore's carbon pricing remains aligned with major trading partners.
key_points.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
key_points.quote: How does Government continuously assess whether Singapore's carbon pricing remains aligned with major trading partners to minimise carbon leakage

key_points.point: Ms Lee Hui Ying asked how Singapore can ensure AI development is climate-aligned.
key_points.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
key_points.quote: How can Singapore ensure AI development is climate-aligned?

key_points.point: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked how Singapore will maintain credibility of its carbon tax policy while keeping industries competitive.
key_points.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
key_points.quote: how will Singapore maintain credibility of our carbon tax policy while ensuring that industries remain competitive

key_points.point: Mr Ng Shi Xuan suggested the National Climate Change Secretariat establish a coordination function to map sector exposure and transferable skills.
key_points.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
key_points.quote: I suggest the National Climate Change Secretariat (NCCS) considers establishing a coordination function to map sector exposure, identify transferable skills and align industries, agencies and employers early.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said climate change is already affecting lives and livelihoods.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: climate change is no longer a future risk. It is already affecting lives and livelihoods, here and now

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said Singapore contributes only 0.1% of global emissions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: Singapore contributes only 0.1% of global emissions.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said the carbon tax has increased to $45 per tonne this year.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: we have increased the carbon tax to $45 per tonne this year.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said the Government is reviewing the carbon tax trajectory for 2028 and beyond and will announce future rates in advance.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: We are therefore reviewing the carbon tax trajectory for 2028 and beyond, and will announce future rates in advance.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said Singapore may position toward the lower end of $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030 if global climate action slows significantly.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: we may need to position ourselves toward the lower end of the previously announced range of $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said households will be supported through additional U-Save rebates.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: We will also support households to manage energy costs through additional U-Save rebates as we have announced.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said Singapore reached its 2030 solar deployment target of two gigawatt-peak ahead of schedule.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: we have reached our 2030 solar deployment target of two gigawatt-peak ahead of schedule

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said 66% of buildings have been greened as of last year, up from 61%.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: We have greened 66% of our buildings as of last year, up from 61% the year before.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said Singapore has signed 10 Implementation Agreements for carbon credits.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: we have signed 10 Implementation Agreements with countries such as Vietnam, Thailand and Peru.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said the fifth carbon credits agreement will be operationalised on 31 March with Thailand.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: we will operationalise our fifth agreement on 31 March with Thailand

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said Singapore announced an award for about two million tonnes of high-integrity nature-based credits from Ghana, Paraguay and Peru.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: we announced the award for about two million tonnes of high-integrity, nature-based credits from projects in Ghana, Paraguay and Peru.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong corrected the green procurement figure to 5%.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: It should be 5%.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said the Government is assessing the proposed Carbon Transition Council and will provide an update.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: We are assessing the proposal and will provide an update in due course.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said Singapore pledged up to US$500 million to FAST-P.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: Singapore has pledged up to US$500 million to FAST-P

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said the Green Investments Partnership under FAST-P achieved its first close with US$510 million in committed capital.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: The Green Investments Partnership under FAST-P has achieved its first close with US$510 million in committed capital

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said a National Adaptation Plan is being developed.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: We are developing a National Adaptation Plan to strengthen resilience across infrastructure, public health, water, food and coastal protection.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said the annual increase in global carbon emissions is now 0.3%.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: The annual increase in global carbon emissions is now at 0.3%

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said MTI will respond on carbon allowances during its Committee of Supply.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: On the carbon allowance, MTI will respond to that issue during MTI's COS.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said Singapore adopts a multi-pronged approach to energy supply and security.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: We adopt a multi-pronged approach to ensure our energy supply and security.

key_points.point: Mr Vikram Nair said Singapore's resident total fertility rate stands at 0.97, a historic low.
key_points.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
key_points.quote: Singapore's latest resident total fertility rate (TFR) stands at 0.97, a historic low.

key_points.point: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre said Singapore's Wealth Gini stands at 0.55.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
key_points.quote: Our Wealth Gini stands at 0.55, higher than our Income Gini and likely an underestimate.

key_points.point: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre proposed that Singapore study the introduction of a Baby Bond.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
key_points.quote: I propose that Singapore study the introduction of a Baby Bond.

key_points.point: Mr Pritam Singh asked whether the Government will look at Employment Pass holders and long-time PR applicants for citizenship.
key_points.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
key_points.quote: Is the Government keen on looking at Employment Pass holders, for example, or individuals or PRs who have been applying many, many years for citizenship

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said the Government is keeping all options open and will take a fresh look at many applicants.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: We are keeping all options open, so we will take a fresh look at many of these applicants.

key_points.point: Mr Gan Kim Yong said assimilability is key.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: the key is really assimilability

key_points.point: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis said banks have been rationalising ATMs and branches at an average rate of 2% annually.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
key_points.quote: banks in Singapore have been rationalising their off-premise automated teller machines (ATMs) and bank branches at an average rate of 2% annually

key_points.point: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis said ATM withdrawals fell by 13.6% from 2018 to 2024, dropping to $55 billion.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
key_points.quote: ATM withdrawals fell by 13.6% from 2018 to 2024, dropping to $55 billion

key_points.point: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis said MAS, HDB and banks should collaborate to identify underserved communities.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
key_points.quote: MAS, HDB and banks should collaborate to actively identify underserved communities

key_points.point: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis hoped the Government would mandate physical merchants to accept cash.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
key_points.quote: I hope that the Government would mandate physical merchants to accept cash in payments

key_points.point: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis asked the Government to affirm its commitment to regular, sustained EQDP funding.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
key_points.quote: Can the Government affirm its commitment to regular, sustained EQDP funding

key_points.point: Miss Rachel Ong said families still report exclusions, higher premiums or rejection for adults with developmental conditions.
key_points.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
key_points.quote: Families still report exclusions, higher premiums or rejection when adults with developmental conditions apply for life or critical illness insurance.

key_points.point: Miss Rachel Ong asked whether the Government will work with MAS and insurers to track anonymised data on disability-related rejections and exclusions.
key_points.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
key_points.quote: will the Government work with MAS and insurers to track anonymised data on disability-related rejections and exclusions

key_points.point: Mr Chee Hong Tat said the goal is a cash-lite society, not a cashless society.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: Our goal is to build a "cash-lite" society, not a cashless society.

key_points.point: Mr Chee Hong Tat said HDB has given the go-ahead for DBS to set up an ATM at Rivervale Shores.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: HDB has given the go-ahead for DBS to proceed to set up this ATM.

key_points.point: Mr Chee Hong Tat said cash should remain an accessible payment option for consumers in Singapore.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: cash should remain an accessible payment option for consumers in Singapore

key_points.point: Mr Chee Hong Tat said MAS is monitoring and may consider making cash acceptance mandatory by law.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: This includes the possibility of making cash acceptance mandatory by law.

key_points.point: Mr Chee Hong Tat said the EQDP aims to develop local fund management capabilities.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: The EQDP aims to develop the local fund management capabilities

key_points.point: Mr Chee Hong Tat said MAS expects insurers to make objective assessments based on reliable information or data relevant to risks.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: MAS expects insurers to make objective assessments of insurance applications based on reliable information or data relevant to the risks

key_points.point: Mr Chee Hong Tat said MAS received one complaint in the past three years relating to insurance coverage for persons with disabilities, compared to eight in 2021 and 2022.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: In the past three years, MAS received one complaint relating to insurance coverage for persons with disabilities, compared to a total of eight complaints in 2021 and 2022.

key_points.point: Mr Chee Hong Tat said MAS will study the suggestion to collect and monitor relevant data from insurers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: to collect and monitor relevant data from the insurers

key_points.point: Mr Foo Cexiang withdrew his cut.
key_points.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
key_points.quote: With that, I would like to withdraw my cut.

what_happens_next: Mr Foo Cexiang withdrew his amendment. The Government will operationalise its fifth carbon credits agreement on 31 March with Thailand, is reviewing the carbon tax trajectory for 2028 and beyond and will announce future rates in advance, and is assessing the proposed Carbon Transition Council and will provide an update in due course. MTI will respond on carbon allowances during its COS. HDB has given the go-ahead for DBS to set up an ATM at Rivervale Shores. MAS will study collecting and monitoring relevant insurance data.
